_source: Ryan Boren's brief, 2026-10-11: Gentle Help Cannabis Farm, in Nature's Contribution, cannabis grown with companion plants; kind, gentle, green, flowering, celebrating the plant; popular sativa, indica and hybrid strains with their THC, CBD and CBN percentages and terpenes; offering bud, rosins and resins, cordage and cloth, companion plants such as herbs and alfalfa, and education; using the space to educate on harm reduction, with Chelsea's work at a dispensary, his own neuromuscular disease, and our Addiction and Harm Reduction entries. Read by tools/make-gentle-help.py.
_strains: Every figure is Leafly's, off each strain's own page, read 2026-10-11: THC and CBD are the medians of the lab results Leafly has for products sold under that name, and the terpenes are its top three, in its order, from labs it certifies. Leafly publishes no CBN for any strain, so the CBN column says so rather than guessing; and the category is Leafly's word, kept because the brief asked for it and the page says why it predicts so little. Weedmaps answered with a bot check and was not read past; AllBud publishes figures with no source and was not used.
_companions: What grows between the cannabis, out of a grower's guide: “Best Companion Plants for Growing Marijuana”, by Joshua Mezher, at A Pot for Pot, a shop that sells grow kits, read 2026-10-11. What each plant is said to do is the guide's claim and is written as the guide's, because a university extension service says research mostly does not back companion-planting claims, and the page says that too. The farm grows them because they are good to grow: most of them are food, and all of them flower. The guide's reason for lemon balm, hiding the smell from the neighbours, is not here.

quotes.said: In general, we found that industry labels are poorly or inconsistently aligned with the underlying chemistry.
We failed to find clear genetic support for commonly referenced Sativa, Indica and Hybrid types as described in online databases.
Many neurodivergent folks have hyper-reactive nervous systems. Anxiety and sensory overwhelm flood the senses. A substance that eases this flood offers relief and escape.
Harm reduction recognizes and honors the myriad of ways survivors cope, recover, and heal.

_careful: The harm-reduction points, each one public health's own, with where it was read. Ours is only the order and the plain words round them; a quotation is the source's own, and a U.S. government page is in the public domain.

careful.head: Edibles take a while, so start low and go slow
careful.says: Colorado sells edibles in servings of 10 milligrams of THC or less. If you do not know how one will affect you, Colorado says to eat less than one serving and wait at least 90 minutes, and up to four hours, before having more.
careful.quote: Take from 30 minutes to 2 hours to feel intoxicating effects, so some people may eat too much, which can lead to poisoning and/or serious injury.

careful.head: Not before driving
careful.says: Colorado says to wait at least six hours after smoking up to 35 milligrams of THC before driving or riding a bike, and at least eight hours after eating up to 18.
careful.quote: If you intend to drive, the safest option is not to use any alcohol or drugs, including cannabis.

careful.head: Not with alcohol, and tell whoever prescribes for you
careful.says: Colorado says cannabis and alcohol together impair you more than either one alone, and to tell your health care provider if you take prescription medicines, because they can interact.

careful.head: Smoke is hard on lungs
careful.says: Eating it, or a vaporiser for flower, keeps smoke out of your lungs, though Colorado says the research on vaporising is not settled yet.
careful.quote: Smoked cannabis, regardless of how it is smoked, can harm lung tissues and cause scarring and damage to small blood vessels.

careful.head: Vape carts only from a licensed store
careful.says: In 2019 and 2020 an outbreak of lung injuries was traced to vaping products, most of them containing THC and bought from friends, family or dealers rather than stores.
careful.quote: Vitamin E acetate is strongly linked to the EVALI outbreak.

careful.head: Concentrates are much stronger
careful.says: Colorado says concentrates can be up to 90 per cent THC, and that making them at home with flammable solvents has caused explosions and deaths.

careful.head: Never synthetic cannabinoids
careful.says: They are not cannabis, whatever the packet says.
careful.quote: Use of synthetic cannabinoids is associated with severe, potentially life-threatening health effects.

careful.head: If you cannot stop being sick
careful.says: Some people who use a lot of cannabis for a long time start vomiting and cannot stop.
careful.quote: CHS only resolves when a person stops using cannabis completely.

careful.head: Locked up, away from children and pets
careful.says: Colorado says to keep cannabis in child-resistant packaging, locked, where children cannot see or reach it, and that vets are seeing more pets that have eaten it. Poison Help is 1-800-222-1222, and 911 if it is serious.

careful.head: In Colorado
careful.says: You have to be 21. Buy only from a licensed store, an ounce at a time; you can have two ounces and give up to two ounces to another adult, never sell it, and never share it with anybody under 21, which is a felony. Not in public, and not on federal land.
